newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Amcor lifts Australian Kiwi sourcing.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Amcor lifts Australian Kiwi sourcing.

text.p: Australian paper and packaging group Amcor Ltd said on Thursday it would eventually source more than half the paper materials for its New Zealand subsidiary Kiwi Packaging from Australia.

Amcor general manager corporate affairs Peter Cairns said the move followed increased competition in the New Zealand market from the entry of privately-held Australian cardboard and paper maker Pratt Industries Ltd's Visy Board divsion.
Amcor previously relied on Carter Holt Harvey Ltd, its main competitor in New Zealand, to supply the liner board and medium board for corrugated boxes.
Cairns told Reuters the move was designed to ensure the New Zealand subsidiary could supply a wider range of boxes to customers.
"The product that we are able to provide from Australia...that Carter at present can't provide, is the product with quite a proportion of waste paper in it," Cairns said.

"Carter certainly make an excellent paper called craft liner which is pretty much entirely made from virgin pulp but the trend is increasingly to incorporate an increasing amount of waste paper," he said.
Boxes using waste paper were cheaper, and put to different uses, such as beer cartons, rather than for packaging fruit.
"With a new competitor coming in we want to be as competitive as we can in every sector of the market," Cairns said.
Amcor began supplying materials from Australia at the start of the calendar year and would increase the amount sourced from Australia during the year.
"The majority of paper in future will come from our own resources in Australia," Cairns said.
He declined to put a more precise figure on the amount, and said it could vary, depending on Australian demand.
In 1995/96 (July/June), Kiwi Packaging recorded sales of A$210 million.
Concerns at Amcor's move has weighed in recent weeks on Carter Holt Harvey's share price, which closed on Thursday at NZ$2.98, down 17 cents from the start of the week.
